subject: Metered vs flat-fee packaging for Azure private offer — channel margin implications
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: procurement@greenwayhealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Azure private offer — packaging question (metered vs flat) and channel margin

Hi Natalie / Greenway procurement team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As we prep the private offer draft I wanted to surface a packaging decision that will materially affect both unit economics and how we structure the reseller/reseller-margin passback in the marketplace flow. In short: should we anchor on a committed annual flat fee (predictable) or a metered usage model (unit-aligned) for your Azure private offer?

Quick context: Greenway expects a 12–18 month migration with headcount-based ingestion spikes early in the first quarter. You’ve indicated procurement prefers predictable spend but engineering wants the flexibility to grow without immediate re-procurement. That tension is why packaging matters.

I attached a draft PO and a simple pricing matrix that lays out a few options. High-level tradeoffs we want to confirm:
- Predictability vs efficiency: Flat fee simplifies finance and commitments; metered can lower initial cost but needs true-up mechanics.
- Marketplace mechanics: Azure private offers allow both metered SKUs and committed (monthly/annual) SKUs, but the channel passback and list-price anchoring behave differently.
- Channel margin handling: If you involve a reseller / MSP, we need to specify commission % and whether it’s taken as a passback on gross invoice or net after Azure fees.

Action items I’m proposing:
1) We propose two options for Greenway’s PO (A and B) and can pilot A for the first 3 months.
2) Confirm whether your accounting needs a list-price anchor on the invoice (affects marketplace display).
3) If you’re involving an MSP/reseller, please share the expected reseller margin range so we can bake it into the PO.

Option summaries are in the pricing_model_matrix.xlsx. Can you confirm availability for a 30-min slot next week to finalize?

Best,
--
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

Attachments: Azure_PO_Draft_v2.pdf (PDF, 1 page); pricing_model_matrix.xlsx (Excel, 1 sheet)

From: Natalie Reyes <natalie.reyes@greenwayhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure private offer — packaging question (metered vs flat) and channel margin

Hi Soojin,

Appreciate the clear framing — that helps. A few answers from procurement side:
- Predictability is preferred for budget planning; a flat annual commitment would be easiest for our finance team.
- That said, we might accept a hybrid if there’s a strong true-up and a cap.
- We are engaging our reseller partner (BlueCrest Solutions). They typically expect a 15% margin on list price for cloud SaaS sales.

Questions:
1) If we do a flat annual commitment, how do you recommend handling an early termination / scale-down in year 1?
2) With a metered approach, how would Azure marketplace handle passback to the reseller (is it a % of invoice or of list price)?

I can do a 30-min call on Tue 9/8 10–11am PT if that works.

Thanks,
Natalie
Natalie Reyes
Senior Procurement Manager
Greenway Health
procurement@greenwayhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 13:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure private offer — packaging question (metered vs flat) and channel margin

So — copying some quick engineering/ops and commercial thoughts inline so we have an internal position before the call: 

(quoted) > Natalie: If we do a flat annual commitment, how do you recommend handling an early termination / scale-down in year 1?

Our suggested commercial guardrails:
- Flat annual commitment: allow a one-time mid-year adjustment (down or up) with a 30-day notice and prorated true-up. Early termination: pro-rated refund on unused committed months but with a minimum 3-month termination fee to protect onboarding costs.
- Metered: recommend a monthly metered SKU with a quarterly true-up and a hard cap set in the private-offer metadata to prevent surprise overruns. Passback to reseller would be defined as a % of the invoiced amount (net of Azure marketplace transaction fees) to make settlement straightforward.

Channel margin specifics: BlueCrest asking ~15% on list price is reasonable. Two ways to model it:
A) Give BlueCrest 15% of list price; Redwood accepts the delta vs net revenue after marketplace fees. Simpler for marketplace payout but inflates list price anchor.
B) Keep list price conservative and set a reseller commission disbursed outside the marketplace (direct rebate) — cleaner for Redwood net rev but adds settlement overhead.

Irene: can you quickly confirm with Legal/Revenue Ops whether option A will create accounting/headroom issues for our side? If not, leaning A for speed (we can reduce list price later if needed).

- Ben

--
Ben Carter
Director, Partner Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Reyes <natalie.reyes@greenwayhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure private offer — packaging question (metered vs flat) and channel margin

Hi Natalie — thanks for the details and for flagging BlueCrest’s expectation. Per our internal alignment (Ben and Irene copied), here are two concrete PO options you can choose from — both modeled in the attached spreadsheet: 

Option A — Committed annual flat fee (recommended for Finance)
- One-year prepaid commitment billed on a single PO via Azure private offer.
- Reseller commission: 15% of list price paid by Azure marketplace to BlueCrest.
- Early termination: prorated refund minus 3 months fee; one-time mid-year adjustment allowed with 30-day notice.
- Advantages: predictability, simplified billing lines for your AP team.
- Caveat: list price anchoring will show higher on marketplace listings; we can include a note in the private-offer description.

Option B — Metered monthly SKU with quarterly true-up (recommended for engineering/usage alignment)
- Monthly metered invoice via Azure; quarterly true-up against committed floors.
- Reseller commission: 15% of invoice (net-of-marketplace-fees) disbursed by Azure marketplace to BlueCrest.
- Hard cap configurable in the offer to avoid overruns.
- Advantages: efficient if usage ramps are uncertain; lower upfront cash.

Next steps I propose for the Tue 9/8 10am PT call:
- Confirm which option (A or B) Greenway prefers.
- If Option A: confirm PO billing name and PO number; we’ll send the Azure private-offer draft for signature.
- If Option B: confirm the cap and desired cadence for true-ups.

We can also propose a hybrid (commit + overage) if you want the predictability with some per-token alignment.

Best,
Soojin
--
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachment: pricing_model_matrix.xlsx (updated with option A/B rows)

From: Natalie Reyes <natalie.reyes@greenwayhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Azure private offer — packaging question (metered vs flat) and channel margin

Soojin / Ben / Irene — thanks, that framing is helpful. We’re going to move forward with Option A (committed annual flat fee) to satisfy budget certainty. A few items we need in the PO before we sign:
- PO needs the billing entity name as: Greenway Health, Inc. and PO number will be 145872.
- Please include the 3-month termination protection language and an explicit statement that BlueCrest will receive 15% commission of list price via Azure marketplace payout.
- Can you also add a 30-day notice clause for mid-year adjustments and define the proration math in the PO appendix?

If you can incorporate those items I’ll route to legal and AP; aim to sign next week. Let’s set a tentative DocuSign send for Wed 9/15 so we can close before the fiscal month-end.

Natalie
